correctness.rationale: For B_q e_j=w_j e_{j+1}, w_j=1 for j<=0 and q^j for j>=1, all weights nonzero, so each n-fold preimage is unique. Its coordinate is x_j when j<=0, x_j/gamma_j for 1<=j<=n, and x_j gamma_{j-n}/gamma_j for j>n, with gamma_j=q^{j(j-1)/2}. Orthogonal squaring yields the exact inverse-norm identity with finite positive-coordinate sum and Gaussian-weighted tail. The n=j preimage zero-coordinate forces |x_j/gamma_j|<=M A^j for any analytic-core chain. Conversely an exponential envelope bounds both finite sum and Gaussian tail uniformly by O(R1^{2n}), constructs compatible backward preimages and proves membership. For x_j=q^{cj(j-1)/2}, c>0, every fixed-order inverse tail exponent is ck²+O_n(k), while the analytic-core rescaled coordinates are subexponential iff c>=1. Finite-support density and 0<c<1 give strict hyperrange containment. Independent exact rational inverse-norm checks used 39 (q,n) cases, not a replacement for the infinite-n proof.

value.rationale: The analytic-core versus hyperrange distinction is central to local spectral theory. For Mbekhta's canonical non-pseudo-Fredholm bilateral shift, an explicit necessary-and-sufficient Gaussian coordinate envelope and sharp c=1 membership threshold give a natural exact operator invariant and concrete dense strict inclusion. It is not merely a guessed numerical example or an arbitrary slice, though its computation uses elementary inverse products.
